podcast.body: Released in 1998, this album was self-released in the United States and continued to be released on Murder Records in Canada after the collapse of The Enclave. Jay Ferguson considers it, along with "Between The Bridges," as almost a double album because they were recorded close together at the same location. "Now it's 1997. And we've recorded Navy Blues. So we just put it out ourselves."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Sloan In Their Own Words: Part 1

podcast.body: This album performed very well for the band, featuring "Money City Maniacs," which remains one of their most recognizable songs and significantly boosted its sales. Chris Murphy considered this album, along with "Between the Bridges," almost a double album due to their close recording proximity and shared recording location. "Navy Blues did really well. We had a song on it called Money City Maniacs, which is still probably our most recognizable song."
